# PR Guard — GitHub Actions Template

An AI-powered PR analysis workflow for Databricks and Python projects.  
Posts a structured comment on every pull request with:

- **AI Summary** — per-PR change description generated by OpenAI, Anthropic, or Databricks
- **Test Results + Coverage** — pytest pass/fail counts, coverage %, and per-file breakdown for changed files
- **Dependency Vulnerabilities** — OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) scan of your `requirements.txt`

The comment is created on the first push and **edited in-place** on subsequent pushes — no spam.

---

## Quick Start

### 1. File layout (already set up in this repo)

```
.github/
├── workflows/
│   └── pr-guard.yml
└── pr-guard/
    ├── pr_guard.py           
    ├── llm_reviewer.py       
    ├── dep_checker.py        
    └── requirements.txt      
```

> All scripts land in `.github/pr-guard/` so they are separate from your project code.

### 2. Set repository Secrets

Go to **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Secrets**.

| Secret | Required when | Description |
|--------|--------------|-------------|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` | OpenAI API key |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` | Anthropic API key |
| `DATABRICKS_HOST` | `LLM_PROVIDER=databricks` | e.g. `https://adb-123.azuredatabricks.net` |
| `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` | `LLM_PROVIDER=databricks` | Databricks personal access token |

### 3. Configure feature flags

Edit the `env:` block in `pr-guard.yml` (or use **Settings → Variables** to override without touching the file):

```yaml
env:
  ENABLE_LLM_SUMMARY: "true"      # AI-generated change summary
  ENABLE_TESTS:       "true"      # pytest + coverage report
  ENABLE_DEP_CHECK:   "true"      # OSV vulnerability scan

  LLM_PROVIDER: "databricks"      # openai | anthropic | databricks
  LLM_MODEL:    "databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct"

  COVERAGE_THRESHOLD: "80"        # warn in comment if coverage drops below this
  DEP_SEVERITIES:    "critical,high,medium,unknown"
  REQUIREMENTS_FILES: "requirements.txt"   # space-separated
```

### 4. Open a pull request

The workflow triggers automatically on `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened` PR events.

---

## Configuration Reference

### Feature Flags

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `ENABLE_LLM_SUMMARY` | `"true"` | Generate an AI summary of the diff |
| `ENABLE_TESTS` | `"true"` | Run pytest and embed results + coverage in the comment |
| `ENABLE_DEP_CHECK` | `"true"` | Scan requirements files for CVEs via OSV |

### LLM Settings

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `"openai"` | `openai`, `anthropic`, or `databricks` |
| `LLM_MODEL` | provider default | Model name (see table below) |
| `MAX_DIFF_CHARS` | `"20000"` | Max characters of diff sent to the LLM |

#### Model names by provider

| Provider | Free / Default | Alternatives |
|----------|---------------|--------------|
| `openai` | `gpt-4o` | `gpt-4o-mini`, `o3-mini` |
| `anthropic` | `claude-opus-5` | `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5` |
| `databricks` | `databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct` | `databricks-dbrx-instruct`, `databricks-mixtral-8x7b-instruct` |

> **Databricks tip:** `databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct` is free for
> Databricks workspace users and requires no external API spend.

### Test + Coverage Settings

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `COVERAGE_THRESHOLD` | `"80"` | Coverage % below which a warning badge (🟡/🔴) is shown |
| `PYTEST_PATHS` | `"tests/"` | Directory or file pattern passed to pytest |
| `COVERAGE_SRC` | `"."` | Source directory measured for coverage |
| `PYTEST_ARGS` | `""` | Extra pytest flags (e.g. `"-x"`, `"-k test_api"`) |

To **block merges** when coverage drops, add `--cov-fail-under=80` to `PYTEST_ARGS`. The workflow uses `continue-on-error: true` on the test step by default so the comment is always posted even if tests fail.

### Dependency Check Settings

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `DEP_SEVERITIES` | `"critical,high,medium,unknown"` | Comma-separated severity levels to report |
| `REQUIREMENTS_FILES` | `"requirements.txt"` | Space-separated list of requirements files |

#### Severity levels

| Level | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `critical` | CVSS ≥ 9.0 or GHSA "CRITICAL" |
| `high` | CVSS ≥ 7.0 or GHSA "HIGH" |
| `medium` | CVSS ≥ 4.0 or GHSA "MODERATE" |
| `low` | CVSS < 4.0 or GHSA "LOW" |
| `unknown` | No CVSS score found in OSV record |

Set `DEP_SEVERITIES: "critical,high"` to suppress medium/low/unknown findings.

## Databricks-Specific Setup

### Using the free Llama 3.3 70B model

1. In your Databricks workspace, ensure the **Foundation Models** serving endpoint is available  
   (Workspace → Machine Learning → Serving — look for `databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct`)
2. Create a personal access token: **User Settings → Access Tokens → Generate**
3. Add to GitHub Secrets:
   - `DATABRICKS_HOST`: your workspace URL (e.g. `https://adb-1234567890.12.azuredatabricks.net`)
   - `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`: the token generated above
4. In `pr-guard.yml`:
   ```yaml
   LLM_PROVIDER: "databricks"
   LLM_MODEL: "databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct"
   ```

### Multi-file requirements (Databricks projects)

Databricks projects often have split requirements. Scan all of them:

```yaml
REQUIREMENTS_FILES: "requirements.txt requirements-dev.txt"
```

---

## How It Works

```
pull_request event
  └── actions/checkout@v4  (full history)
  └── pip install requirements.txt + .github/pr-guard/requirements.txt
  └── [if ENABLE_TESTS] pytest → pytest_report.json + coverage.json
  └── gh pr diff → pr_diff.txt
  └── python .github/pr-guard/pr_guard.py
        ├── [if ENABLE_LLM_SUMMARY] llm_reviewer.py → AI summary (OpenAI/Anthropic/Databricks)
        ├── [if ENABLE_TESTS]       parse pytest_report.json + coverage.json
        ├── [if ENABLE_DEP_CHECK]   dep_checker.py  → OSV scan (two-phase: batch + detail)
        └── post or update PR comment
```

### What the PR comment looks like

```
🛡️ PR Guard Analysis
┌──────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PR       │ #42 — Add Databricks feature store client │
│ Author   │ @krishna                                  │
│ Commit   │ abc1234                                   │
│ Features │ LLM (databricks) · tests + coverage · ... │
└──────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┘

🤖 AI Summary
  ### What changed ...
  ### Why it matters ...
  ### Review focus areas ...

---

🧪 Test Results
  ✅ All tests passed
  ┌──────────┬───────┐      Coverage
  │ Passed   │  42   │      ┌──────────────────┬───────┐
  │ Failed   │   0   │      │ 🟢 Total         │ 83.2% │
  │ Skipped  │   1   │      │ Statements       │   128 │
  │ Duration │ 5.3s  │      │ Missing          │    22 │
  └──────────┴───────┘      └──────────────────┴───────┘

  Coverage for changed files
  ┌──────────────────────────┬──────────┬────────────────┐
  │ File                     │ Coverage │ Missing lines  │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────┼────────────────┤
  │ app/services/client.py   │ 🟢 91.2% │ 45, 78         │
  │ app/handlers/webhook.py  │ 🔴 61.0% │ 12, 34, 56 … │
  └──────────────────────────┴──────────┴────────────────┘

---

📦 Dependency Vulnerabilities
  | Severity | Package | Installed | Fix | CVE |
  ...
```

### Dependency Scanner (OSV)

The dep checker queries the [OSV API](https://osv.dev) directly — no subprocess, no pip resolver, no installation required:

- **Phase 1**: `POST /v1/querybatch` — matches all pinned packages in one call
- **Phase 2**: `GET /v1/vulns/{id}` — concurrent detail fetch (10 connections max)

Only **exact-pinned** packages (`pkg==1.2.3`) are checked. Loose constraints (`>=`, `~=`) are skipped because OSV requires an exact version.

## Disabling for a PR

Add `[skip pr-guard]` anywhere in the PR title to skip the analysis for that PR:

```yaml
# In pr-guard.yml, add this condition to the job:
if: |
  github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
  !contains(github.event.pull_request.title, '[skip pr-guard]')
```

---

## Troubleshooting

### "GH_TOKEN is not set"
The workflow passes `github.token` automatically. If you see this error, check that `permissions.pull-requests: write` is in the workflow.

### "OSV batch query failed"
The runner has no internet access to `api.osv.dev`. Check your org's network egress rules or disable dep check: `ENABLE_DEP_CHECK: "false"`.

### "DATABRICKS_HOST and DATABRICKS_TOKEN must be set"
Both secrets must be present in the repo. Verify under **Settings → Secrets**.

### LLM call times out
Increase `MAX_DIFF_CHARS` to reduce the prompt size, or switch to a faster model (`gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct`).

### Comment not appearing on the PR
Check the Actions run logs for `[pr_guard] Comment URL:`. If absent, look for an HTTP error from the GitHub API. Verify the workflow has `pull-requests: write` permission.

## File Reference

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `workflow.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow — triggers, permissions, steps |
| `scripts/pr_guard.py` | Main orchestrator — reads diff, calls features, posts comment |
| `scripts/llm_reviewer.py` | LLM provider adapters (OpenAI / Anthropic / Databricks) |
| `scripts/dep_checker.py` | OSV-based dependency vulnerability scanner |
| `scripts/requirements.txt` | Python dependencies for the scripts |
